rules.rationale: Highly electronegative halide anions give deep valence bands and large ionic gaps in experimental compounds.
Main-group oxides lack partially filled d bands, so their gaps stay wide unlike transition-metal oxides.
Light elements have compact orbitals, weak spin-orbit effects, and low polarizability, all favoring wider gaps.
Partially filled d manifolds introduce mid-gap states and narrow conduction-band offsets, reducing measured band gaps.

skill.hypothesis: Encodes wide-gap ionic chemistry independently of the source task: electronegative closed-shell anions with light main-group cations. Fails if the pool's halide and light-oxide subsets are small, or if d0 transition-metal oxides dominate the top of the target distribution.
